paths.description: Homepage and primary news index; desktop/mobile, preferences, accessibility, performance, network, privacy, discoverability and memory.
World section listing template representing section/collection pages.
Representative editorial article/detail template selected from the live homepage.
Primary search/results journey using a representative climate query.
Authentication/account entry journey reached from the masthead.

findings.summary: The public news experience is locked to a light palette even when the user requests dark mode.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light capture, the page declares meta color-scheme=light, and computed body background remains white.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and define preference-driven surface, text, border, image-treatment, and browser-chrome colors with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: A consent panel obscures a large share of the primary news content on every fresh load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile first-load screenshots show the “Manage privacy preferences” panel covering the lower 25% of desktop and most of the 360px viewport before any user action.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise the first-layer notice, preserve equally prominent accept/reject choices, and make the content usable without a viewport-dominating interruption.

findings.summary: The homepage overflows horizontally at a 360px viewport.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout primitive measured scrollWidth 627px against clientWidth 360px, producing 267px of horizontal overflow despite a valid viewport meta tag.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove minimum/fixed widths from the homepage shell and consent UI, use intrinsic sizing and min-width:0 in grid/flex children, and regression-test at 320–400px.

findings.summary: Reusable components expose no container-query adaptation in the loaded homepage or section CSS.
findings.evidence: The DOM/CSS probe found no @container or container-type signal while the same card/navigation patterns appear across differently sized regions.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable card, stream, and navigation components containment and use size-aware container queries where their layout depends on available component width.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus can be effectively invisible and several mobile targets are too tightly spaced.
findings.evidence: A focused primary news link matched :focus-visible but computed to a transparent 2px outline with no box shadow. Lighthouse also identified nine footer target-size groups.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a high-contrast :focus-visible ring with offset and increase target padding/spacing to at least a 24px minimum safe area, preferably 44px for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance is far outside good user-centric thresholds on both audited templates.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured homepage LCP 32.1s, FCP 13.4s, TBT 2,800ms and performance 0.26; World measured LCP 29.8s, FCP 8.9s and TBT 1,670ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat LCP and main-thread work as release blockers: profile the LCP chain, remove non-critical startup work, prioritise the true LCP asset, and set measurable CWV budgets.

findings.summary: The World section shifts substantially after load.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout observer recorded CLS 0.253, including a single 0.196 shift around 16.8s; Lighthouse independently measured non-zero CLS.
findings.suggestedFix: Identify the late stream/banner/font insertion responsible, reserve its final geometry, and use stable font fallbacks and intrinsic media dimensions.

findings.summary: Heavy script execution blocks the main thread during startup.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded 13 long tasks, a 516.6ms longest task and 899.6ms TBT; Lighthouse attributed 7.5s to script evaluation and measured 2.8s TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Break startup tasks into yieldable chunks, defer ad/video/account integrations until needed, and move suitable processing off the main thread.

findings.summary: The homepage performs an exceptionally large, eager network load with many critical-style candidates.
findings.evidence: The HAR captured 385 requests and 12.5MB transferred, including 35 stylesheets and 239 scripts; parser-inserted high-priority video CSS and font/global styles form a large startup chain.
findings.suggestedFix: Restrict preloads and parser-blocking styles to above-the-fold needs, lazy-load video/player bundles, consolidate critical CSS, and apply effective immutable caching.

findings.summary: Large amounts of JavaScript and CSS are unused on the initial homepage view.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 1,244KiB unused JavaScript and 85KiB unused CSS; examples include 143KiB wasted hls.js and 72KiB wasted Lottie code.
findings.suggestedFix: Route- and interaction-split video, animation, account, and advertising modules; load each only when its component becomes relevant.

findings.summary: Video posters and composite feeds contain accessibility-tree errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found seven poster images without alt and a role=feed missing required child roles on the homepage; the World template also fails required ARIA parent/child relationships and list semantics.
findings.suggestedFix: Give meaningful posters concise alt (or alt="" when decorative), implement complete feed/tab semantics, and ensure lists contain valid list children.

findings.summary: Footer controls do not provide sufficient touch target size or spacing.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified nine target-size groups; examples include footer links whose safe clickable diameter is 15–18px, below the 24px audit floor.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase link block padding and row/column gaps so each target has at least 24px unobstructed space, with larger targets for common mobile actions.

findings.summary: Both audited templates emit runtime and network errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured five homepage errors and three World errors, including a production React hydration error #418, FedCM failures, and repeated 404 resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Eliminate the hydration mismatch, gate identity calls on usable FedCM state, and remove or repair missing resource requests.

findings.summary: Most homepage images omit intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 25 of 29 images without width/height attributes, while the World layout showed a large late shift.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height or an equivalent stable aspect ratio for every responsive image before it loads.

findings.summary: Deprecated unload handling prevents back/forward cache restoration and large first-party bundles lack valid source maps.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found an unload listener in adslot code, a BFCache failure, missing source maps, and DevTools inspector issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace unload with pagehide/visibilitychange where needed, preserve BFCache eligibility, and publish valid production source maps to the intended access boundary.

findings.summary: Some homepage links are rendered as anchors without href values.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 28 non-crawlable anchor instances (a.tpl-lbl without href), even though the page otherwise server-renders 98% of content.
findings.suggestedFix: Render navigation as real anchors with stable href values; reserve buttons for actions that do not navigate.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP settings weaken otherwise strong HTTPS transport.
findings.evidence: The headers probe found CSP allowing unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval. Cookie inspection found nyt-gdpr and nyt-geo without Secure and six cookies using SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsafe-eval/unsafe-inline through nonces or hashes, set Secure on all HTTPS cookies, and use Lax/Strict unless cross-site delivery is required.

findings.summary: The fresh-load privacy and tracking footprint is disproportionate for reading the front page.
findings.evidence: The consent UI names 336 vendors; the tracker probe observed 24 third-party origins and known ad trackers, while the HAR attributed 147 requests and 10.1MB to origins classified as third-party.
findings.suggestedFix: Default to a minimal non-personalised stack, remove vendors without direct reader value, delay optional tags until explicit consent, and batch first-party measurement.

findings.summary: Referrer policy is not explicitly set and the permissions policy only disables browsing topics.
findings.evidence: The headers probe found no Referrer-Policy; Permissions-Policy was present but limited to browsing-topics=(), while HSTS, nosniff, and X-Frame-Options were correctly configured.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a deliberate Referrer-Policy such as strict-origin-when-cross-origin and enumerate denied-by-default powerful features in Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Image markup does not expose an efficient, stability-friendly asset baseline.
findings.evidence: The image primitive classified all 29 image URLs as legacy-format paths, found 25 missing intrinsic dimensions and one missing responsive source set; delivery may negotiate WebP, but markup remains inconsistent.
findings.suggestedFix: Standardise responsive srcset/sizes, intrinsic dimensions, and negotiated AVIF/WebP delivery for all editorial and decorative image variants.

findings.summary: The initial page performs substantial work unrelated to immediate reading.
findings.evidence: The HAR shows 239 scripts and 7.3MB media transfer, while Lighthouse identifies 1.24MB unused JS and 7.5s script evaluation.
findings.suggestedFix: Deprioritise background analytics/ad work, load media only after user intent or viewport proximity, and remove redundant startup execution.

findings.summary: Autoloaded media and third-party delivery dominate the front-page byte budget.
findings.evidence: Two 1080p video segments account for about 7.3MB; total transferred bytes are 12.5MB and third-party-classified origins account for 10.1MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not fetch video segments before playback intent, use poster-only placeholders, and enforce per-template third-party/media byte budgets.

findings.summary: The homepage has a very large initial JavaScript heap/object population for a news index.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contains 1,956,211 nodes and 120.1MB self size, including 385k native nodes, 554k objects and 113k closures.
findings.suggestedFix: Virtualise/defer below-fold modules, avoid hydrating static content, unload inactive media/ad components, and profile dominant native/object retainers.

taskList.title: Make LCP and main-thread budgets release-blocking, then remove eager video/ad/account startup work
Reduce the pre-consent vendor, tracker, script and data footprint
Fix mobile homepage overflow, focus visibility and touch spacing
Repair image, feed, tab and list accessibility semantics
Reserve late section geometry and intrinsic media space to eliminate CLS
Harden CSP, cookies, referrer and permissions policies
Eliminate runtime errors, deprecated unload handling and BFCache blockers
Restore href values on all navigational anchors
Add a complete preference-driven dark palette
Reduce the hydrated DOM and heap footprint of below-fold modules
